title: Release sync swaps while the daemon runs
goal: The Windows release sync helper completes a swap while the installed daemon runs. Since sockfix2 every leaf service runs in the daemon's kill-on-close job, so stopping the daemon takes its leaves down and a leaf listed for stopping may already be gone; the helper threw 'Cannot find a process' and aborted the v0.21.53 upgrade on the CEO laptop. The helper now stops daemon-start processes first and the services after, treats a listed process that is confirmed gone (no such process, or its PID now names a later process) as stopped, pins each process by handle before checking its identity and stopping it, bounds every wait, and still fails on any other error such as access denied. Every other guarantee is unchanged: refuse while a non-service client runs, preserve the previous executable, roll back on a failed move, never touch another installation's processes. The regression itself had not run on Windows since 2026-11-01: tests/release_workflow.rs compiled it for unix only, where it checks shell syntax, so cargo test --test release_workflow ran 0 tests on the Windows gate. It now runs natively on Windows through Windows PowerShell, bounded at 300 s, finds Git for Windows bash from git itself (PATH bash.exe can be the WSL launcher), and must report its PASS line.
acceptance: cargo test --offline --locked --test release_workflow passes: the Windows promotion regression runs a daemon fixture that puts a service-run copy of itself in a kill-on-close Job Object, and swap succeeds with the daemon running, installs the new image, preserves the previous one, stops the owned daemon and its leaf, and leaves the other installation's daemon and leaf running. Against the previous helper the same test fails with 'Cannot find a process with the process identifier'.
